description: '''Rock doido''' ({{Literal translation|crazy rock}}) is a Brazilian musical genre that emerged in the outskirts of [[Belém]], [[Pará]], as a sped-up offshoot of [[Tecno brega|tecnobrega]] in the late 2000s. It is characterized by fast electronic beats, usually close to 180 [[Tempo|beats per minute]], achieved by speeding up songs from genres such as [[Funk carioca|funk]], [[axé]], [[forró]], and [[reggaeton]], combined with original compositions produced at the same tempo. The name, which bears no relation to [[rock music]], also refers to the peak moment of ''aparelhagem'' parties — traditional popular events in Pará that bring together large sound systems, stage structures, light panels, and pyrotechnics — and, by extension, to the events themselves held in this format.
